% note: Pairs: unordered pairs of wrong samples on the same puzzle and shape. Agreeing pairs give the identical official answer (a sample with no answer or whose official format is not ok never agrees). Repeat share: agreeing pairs divided by pairs, pooled over the puzzles kept (the puzzles with at least two wrong samples).
% note: No pairs: no puzzle had two wrong samples, so the share is undefined.
% note: Both shapes: the chains' and the pieces' pairs and agreeing pairs added together, and the share is agreeing pairs over pairs; no count of puzzles is stamped for these rows, so Puzzles kept shows a dash.
% note: The Study~1 Haiku-medium rows are Study~1's locked, pre-specified descriptive values; the post hoc recount gives the same counts (checked when the table is built). Every other row is post hoc.
% note: The Study~1b Haiku-medium rows go beyond the settings this post hoc analysis was defined to cover (Haiku-max, Haiku-high and Haiku-xhigh in Study~1b, and Haiku-max on Study~1's 3 samples); the same post hoc recount computed them, and they are shown as the same-set medium-effort baseline for the higher efforts.
% note: Rows differ in study, puzzle set, length and samples per puzzle; a share from few pairs or few puzzles is fragile. Setting rows side by side, above all across the two studies, is our reading, not a test.
% note: Exploratory, no causal claim: the table does not show that repeated wrong answers cause or prevent anything.
